title: Strangling the legacy (strangler fig) and coexistence

videos.script: Every large company has a system like Coleta. {{coleta}} It is thirty years old. It pays nineteen hundred farms every month. And the one person who really understands it retires in 2028. The obvious plan is to write a new one and switch over on a weekend. {{bigbang}} This lesson is about why that plan fails, and what to do instead. A strangler fig grows around its host tree, until the host is gone. {{fig}} You can do the same to a legacy system. You put something in front of it, and move its work across one capability at a time. Coleta has no front door, so you stand in the path of its files and read its journal. {{intercept}} You translate at the border, so the new system does not inherit the old one's shape. Then you live for months with both systems running, and one owner for every piece of data. {{coexist}} And at the end you switch the old machine off, on a date somebody wrote down. {{off}} Progress is not what you built. It is what you turned off.
